title: Could the NMDS + Clustering method be used to produce heuristic ideas?

lists.name: Hypothesis
lists.of: elements which, illustratively, could be used in Step A-1 below

lists.name: Procedure
items: Step one: NMDS-weight inter set (i.e. subset) by Scaling relation weights or agency to which suggests observers might get proximity to get question likely interested in.
Step two: Apply NMDS-weight same set but this time by Scaling relation (degree) such as “degree to which some item (or group) suggests associated ideas (in feeling) strongly or faintly interested.”

Step three: Now the two data-sets could be used to have a computer automatically produce a semantic map (or a hybrid NMDS + clusteranalytic map), or rather a printout of a questionnaire set of clusters arranged in a concentric-distributive order, which would represent probable generally revolutionary or more promising generic metaconcepts (in a virtual or actual way) and contained within them of clustered concrete concepts.

(Optional) Step four: All of the above could be taken further in various ways, an important example of which would be: By intermapping the same ideative NMDS data-sets, maps, clustering either onto or via other better (or merely different) ideative dimensions.

notes: For instance, if “Congeneric shape species” was what finally resulted, or purportedly the above Step 1–3, then the almost “Universal Generic Concepts” could be intermapped into the above, via some ideonomy MDS model, to produce a more sophisticated genealogy of partial sets, idea maps, concept sets, cluster mappings, cluster hierarchies, etc.; say for heuristic or theoretical purposes. What all that which I have merely suggested here offers could be a somewhat universally heuristic means—but since such a divine quote presupposes AI (artificial intelligence): The reason I think is that I have personally discerned and shown that performing many of these operations repetitively, in variously alternate combinations, may powerfully provoke and generate gestalt-like metaconcepts.
